calibration.note: Two scorers on the same player in the same window may differ by at most 1 on any metric. Anything wider means the anchor is ambiguous — rewrite the anchor, do not average the scores.

anchors.1: Loses every race off the line. Gets beaten to loose pucks inside 10 feet.
anchors.3: Wins some races. Acceleration is adequate at current level, exposed a level up.
anchors.5: Separates from checkers on the first push. Wins contested pucks through acceleration alone.

anchors.1: Turns wide, glides through changes of direction, falls off edges under contact.
anchors.3: Functional edges. Tight turns available but not used under pressure.
anchors.5: Changes direction without losing speed. Holds edges through contact in traffic.

anchors.1: Plays a step behind. Receives pucks stopped, exits shifts late.
anchors.3: Matches game pace in stretches, drops off late in shifts.
anchors.5: Plays faster than the game around them. Forces opponents into rushed decisions.

anchors.1: Loses the puck on first contact. Faces pressure directly.
anchors.3: Protects along the wall. Struggles when pressured from two sides.
anchors.5: Uses body, angles and leverage to hold pucks under real pressure and still make a play.

anchors.1: Head down through the middle. Puck gets stripped in crowded ice.
anchors.3: Comfortable in open ice, simplifies in traffic.
anchors.5: Manipulates sticks and bodies in tight. Creates ice where there was none.

anchors.1: No shoulder checks. Discovers pressure after receiving.
anchors.3: Scans on the rush, stops scanning under forecheck.
anchors.5: Consistent pre-scan. Knows the first option before the puck arrives.

anchors.1: Forces low-percentage plays or defaults to rimming it out.
anchors.3: Makes the available pass. Rarely makes the better one.
anchors.5: Finds the second and third option. Passes to the correct side of the stick.

anchors.1: Reacts to plays after they develop. Frequently out of position.
anchors.3: Reads standard situations, late on broken plays.
anchors.5: Anticipates. Arrives where the puck is going without being sent there.

anchors.1: Gaps off, gives up the blue line, angles attackers to the middle.
anchors.3: Maintains gap on the rush, loses it on delays and regroups.
anchors.5: Kills speed early. Angles attackers to the wall every time.

anchors.1: Stick in the air or on the wrong side. Retrievals become turnovers.
anchors.3: Active stick in lanes. Retrievals are safe but slow.
anchors.5: Stick takes away the intended play. Retrieves under forecheck and exits clean.

anchors.1: Avoids contested pucks. Arrives second and stops.
anchors.3: Competes when the battle is even, disengages when it isn't.
anchors.5: Wins battles against bigger players through leverage and second effort.

anchors.1: Plays the perimeter. No inside presence on either end.
anchors.3: Goes to the net when the play sends them there.
anchors.5: Lives inside the dots. Takes contact to hold ice in front.
